A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SMI-EDITOR and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–X. Corresponding material can be reliably matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining, molecular property prediction, ablation, and retrosynthesis experiments, including appendix results and five-fold cross-validation.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including property prediction, retrosynthesis, and cross-validation outcomes.

M1.justification: The encoder, molecular fragmentation, editing heads, and dual deletion objective are unchanged. The SMI-EDITOR-Cor and encoder-decoder SMI-EDITOR-Gen variants were already described in v1.

E1.justification: Downstream dataset and task coverage is unchanged. However, v2 Appendix J newly specifies pretraining data from Ross et al. (2022), whereas v1 provides no J-specific attribution and its general settings cite Zhou et al. (2023). The PDFs do not establish whether the underlying corpus changed or this corrects its documentation.

E2.justification: Table 8 removes Galactica from the DeepChem-split comparison. The remaining comparators, including the separate SMI-GPT comparisons in Table 9 and retrosynthesis baselines in Table 15, are unchanged. Appendix J still mentions outperforming Galactica.

E3.justification: Appendix G revises the reported pretraining compute setup from four Tesla A40 GPUs for about two days to four RTX3090 GPUs for about one day, aligning with Appendix Q.2. This is a reported setting correction, not evidence of rerunning; update budgets, model sizes, splits, metrics, and fine-tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The fragment and editing-operation ablations, masking/drop-ratio analyses, scaling studies, compute-matched comparison, molecular perturbations, and case studies all existed in v1 and retain their evidence in v2.

E5.justification: Both versions report five evaluations per checkpoint in Appendices E–F, the same parenthetical uncertainty values for retained Table 8 entries, and identical five-fold results, means, and standard deviations in Table 17. No statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Table 8 deletes Galactica's six ROC-AUC scores and its 69.5 mean. Retained benchmark scores and plotted findings are unchanged, including SMI-EDITOR's means of 77.8 in Table 1 and 85.2 in Table 8. Appendix G also revises elapsed training time, without establishing a same-setting speedup.

T1.justification: The editing-policy definitions, Levenshtein expert-action formulations, and loss equations in Section 3 and Appendix B are unchanged. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about MLM saturation, fragment-level semantic learning, edit-based pretraining, scalability, and downstream performance. The code-release footnote does not alter these scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of saturation, fragment semantics, molecular-weight confounding in ESOL, and computational overhead are retained. The encoder-only applicability boundary and explanations of unsuccessful variants also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release location on page 1 and a pretraining-data attribution in Appendix J. Appendix G's hardware/runtime revision resolves its inconsistency with the existing Appendix Q.2 report of four RTX3090 GPUs and 24.6 hours. The PDFs alone do not verify the repository's availability.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds five cited works: Lin et al. (2023), Zheng et al. (2024), Hayes et al. (2025), and Yang et al. (2024a, 2024b). These modestly expand the surrounding literature; the central positioning relative to SMILES MLMs and edit-based models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates the publication header, corrects the Appendix A heading, lightly expands related-work prose, and fixes Appendix S's erroneous table references. The main narrative and appendix sequence remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing displays shift with revised spacing, including Figure 10, Figure 12, Table 9, and Table 16 moving across pages. Table 8 loses one row, while graphical content is retained. A stray 'www.' appears beside Figure 3 in v2.

improvement.justification: The code-access pointer, reconciled hardware/runtime account, and corrected table references provide a limited improvement in reproducibility information and navigation. Removing Galactica's results while retaining the comparison claim weakens Appendix J, but the central comparisons and separate SMI-GPT evaluation remain intact. The ambiguous corpus attribution establishes no additional scientific improvement.
